passages.quote:
The Creative and Cultural National Lottery and Grant in Aid funders* (The Funders) across the UK believe that all professionals working in the creative industries and culture sector deserve fair pay, safe working conditions and opportunities to develop and progress. We are therefore committed to upholding the principles of Good and Fair Work, both as employers and in our creative and cultural funding programmes.

Good (or Fair) Work in the creative sectors was defined in the Creative Industries Policy and Evidence Centre’s Good Work Review, and encompasses these core principles:

fair reward, terms and conditions

a balance of security and flexibility

autonomy and personal fulfilment

skill use, development and progression

agency, voice and representation

a healthy, respectful, safe and inclusive work environment

We will work closely with partners, funded organisations, and member representative bodies to support understanding and adoption of Good and Fair Work by organisations across the sector, and will incorporate these principles in our funding conditions and agreements where relevant.

As set out in the Industrial Strategy, delivering good jobs is integral to sustainable economic growth. This statement builds on DCMS’ commitment in the Creative Industries Sector Plan to support the industry’s work to deliver the Good Work Review action plan, as well as the work of our recently appointed Freelance Champions. The Creative Industries Jobs Plan, being published later this month, will set out how government, business and trade unions will work together to collectively address the workforce needs in the sector. Over the next three years, we will tackle workforce challenges to build a resilient, fit-for-the-future workforce including by improving job quality, retention and progression.

*Arts Council England, ALBA Chruthachail, Arts Council of Wales, Youth Music, Creative Wales, BFI and DCMS
